subject: Enterprise burst capacity request — approval path and pre-warm plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Enterprise burst capacity request — initial intake

Team,

Quick heads-up: Skyloft (strategic media customer) just sent a signed MPA amendment that includes a short-term burst reservation for dedicated GPU capacity to support a one-week high-throughput encoding/query window for their new personalization pipeline. Procurement attached the MPA and a completed capacity request form (attached).

High-level:
- Window: 2027-07-05 00:00 UTC through 2027-07-12 23:59 UTC (7 days)
- Request: 40 x A100-equivalent slots pre-warmed, with ability to autoscale +20% on demand
- Models: mix of LLaMA-2-70B and a smaller reranker; token distribution and QPS in the attached spreadsheet
- Revenue: committed MPA amendment (see DocuSign link) + overage billing per committed unit

Need: please confirm the approval path and ops lead time for pre-warming. My asks:
1) Product: any red flags on model compatibility or required quantization profiles? (Lauren)
2) Sales/Finance: confirm billing path and whether we need any credit hold or prepayment (Ben)
3) Engineering Ops: lead time for pre-warm and suggested pre-warm steps / runbook (Hannah)

Attachments: MPA_SOW_Skyloft_v3.pdf, skyloft_capacity_request_form.xlsx

I recommend we lock the reservation no later than 2027-06-14 to guarantee hardware; customer is pushing for guaranteed capacity.

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Account Strategy, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise burst capacity request — initial intake

Thanks Marcus — reviewed the attachments. Quick clarifying questions before I sign off on product constraints:

- Can Ben confirm the expected steady-state and peak QPS per model? The spreadsheet shows token volumes but not per-second distribution. That will determine batch sizing and KV cache memory pressure.
- Are both models being served from the same GPU flavor (A100)? Any requirement for mixed-precision or strict FP16-only inference? If they want INT8 quant, we need to validate accuracy on the customer prompt set.
- Latency SLOs: does Skyloft expect p50 < 100ms? p95 < 500ms? That materially changes the autoscaler policy we propose.
- Fallback policy: do they require a hard SLA (no fallback) or can we automatically route to a slower but cheaper variant if capacity is exhausted?

Operationally, a few notes:
- Pre-warm: for 40 slots we should request a staged warm: 10/10/20 over 24 hours to allow image pulls and kernel selection tuning.
- KV cache priming: we should collect a 48-hour sample workload (Ben, can you get a sample trace?) or we'll rely on synthetic priming which is less efficient.

If we can get QPS and precision requirements today, I'll provide a short product sign-off and list of model variants to allow.

- Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@skyloft.ai>, procurement@skyloft.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise burst capacity request — initial intake

Looping Sarah from Skyloft to confirm a couple items and share the DocuSign flow.

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround on the amendment. A few clarifications for the team:
- Peak QPS: we expect ~1,800 combined QPS at peak (approx 1,500 for 70B runtime calls, 300 for reranker) during campaign hours.
- Precision: customer prefers FP16 with a conservative INT8 profile for cost-savings; they are OK with a short validation run if needed.
- Latency target: soft SLO p50 ~120ms, p95 ~450ms. Hard SLA not required; they'd accept fallback to a smaller variant with prior notice.
- Trace/sample: attaching a 72-hour anonymized trace (refer to the attached spreadsheet).

DocuSign: the MPA amendment has been routed and shows as "Pending signature"; link below to embedded signing. They want billing to be charged to the existing enterprise contract; no prepayment, but procurement will approve invoicing terms in the amendment.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/embeddedSigning/123456789

Ben

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise burst capacity request — initial intake

Thanks — got the QPS and precision guidance from Ben. Ops notes and preliminary timeline below:

Pre-warm plan (high level):
- T-7 days (2027-06-28): confirm reservation and allocate 40 slots in the us-west region.
- T-6 days: stage bootstrap images to nodes (rolling 10/10/20 as Lauren suggested).
- T-5 days: kernel + Triton tuning sweep using 12-hour synthetic traffic (we will run both FP16 and INT8 fast validation).
- T-3 days: KV cache priming against anonymized trace (Ben's 72-hour sample).
- T-1 day: dry-run with mirrored traffic at 60% peak for 2 hours.

Lead time: minimum 10 business days to guarantee hardware and complete tuning; we can do an expedited 5-day path but that increases risk of p95 regressions.

Autoscale exception request:
- Default autoscaler caps at +10% burst for Dedicated pools. To support +20% we need an ops exception and a temporary policy override (requires Product approval + Finance signoff for capacity billing). If approved, we will attach an automatic fallback to pre-configured cheaper variants after a 5-minute graceful period.

Runbook actions (attachment: prewarm-runbook.md) include explicit escalation contacts and roll-back steps.

I can own the orchestration if we get product and finance approvals by 2027-06-14.

— Hannah

Hannah Schmitt
Principal SRE, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Enterprise burst capacity request — initial intake

Appreciate the fast responses — summarizing next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Product (Lauren): confirm model variant allowance for INT8 fast-validate and sign product constraints doc by 2027-06-10.
2) Finance/Sales (Ben): confirm invoicing path and mark the amendment as approved in HubSpot by 2027-06-12. Ben to follow up on procurement questions with Sarah.
3) Ops (Hannah): proceed with reservation request (40 slots) and pre-warm schedule once product + finance approvals are in. Ops to aim for the 10-business-day path; expedite only with explicit risk acceptance.

I'll follow up with Sarah/procurement and coordinate a quick cross-functional call if approvals slip past 2027-06-12.

Marcus
